properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 11:36AM PDT until October 23 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Northeastern Lassen County and Surprise valley in
California, and northern Washoe County and northwestern Pershing
County in Nevada. The watch area includes the Biscar and S1-Vya
burn scars.

* WHEN...Through 5 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Small creeks and streams may flood rural roads. Increased
sediment transport from burn scars may clog culverts and ditches.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Storm total rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches, locally 2 inches or
more, is possible through through early Friday. Heavier rain this
afternoon and evening may briefly exceed 0.5 inch per hour.
Runoff may linger overnight.
- Vulnerable locations include remote ranches within and near the
Biscar and S1-Vya burn scars, downstream drainages, and culverts
along US-395 from Stoney Creek Road north to Rye Patch Road.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Montrose, CO; San Miguel, CO
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 12:31PM MDT until October 22 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...
Southeastern Montrose County in west central Colorado...

* Until 330 PM MDT.

* At 1231 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Heavy
rainfall rates are occurring on already saturated ground as this
area has received between 1 and 2 inches of rain over the last 24
hours. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Norwood, Sawpit, Placerville and Fall Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Highway 145 between Norwood and Sawpit is prone to rockslides and
mudslides in heavy rain. Stay alert for rocks and debris on roads,
and avoid driving on flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and steep
to very steep wind-driven seas 8 to 11 ft.

* WHERE...All areas.

evening. For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 8 PM this
evening to 8 AM PDT Saturday. For the Small Craft Advisory,
from 11 AM Friday to 8 AM PDT Saturday.

damage vessels. Bar crossings will become especially

properties.areaDesc: Los Angeles, CA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:24AM PDT until October 22 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
FFWLOX

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Los Angeles County in southwestern California...
Including central and southern parts of the Bridge Burn Scar.

* Until 200 PM PDT.

* At 1124 AM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is
0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Rock slides, mud slides, and minor debris flows are
possible.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. Rock slides, mud slides, and
minor debris flows.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
San Dimas, Glendora, Pomona, La Verne and Claremont. Central and
southern Bridge Burn Scar.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Follow directions of emergency management, law enforcement, and fire
agency officials.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 12:23PM MDT until October 22 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 330 PM MDT.

* At 1223 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen over the last 24 hours. Heavy
rainfall rates due to thunderstorms are falling over this already
saturated area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Arboles and Chimney Rock.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Highway 151 from Arboles to the intersection of 160 near Chimney Rock
is prone to rockslides and mudslides in heavy rain. Stay alert for
rocks and debris on roads, and avoid driving on flooded roads. Find
an alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
New Harmony, Kanarraville, Kolob Canyon and Hamilton Fort.

This includes the following highways...
Utah Route 56 between mile markers 46 and 53. Interstate 15 between
mile markers 38 and 56.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 12:18PM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by thunderstorms and excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Western Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1212 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen over
the last 24 hours.
- This includes but is not limited to the following streams...
Vallecito Creek, La Plata River, Animas River and many creeks and
tributaries that feed into these rivers.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, La Plata, Falfa, Hesperus, Bondad, Breen, Mayday, Kline,
Marvel, Redmesa and Vallecito.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.
